title: Radio: Generator Elevator Down, Then Staffing on 1:3 All Night

lines.text: House Sup, Security post 3. One of the two generator cars just faulted between 5 and 6. Nobody inside, I checked the camera. Panel shows door zone fault, out of service.

House Sup, post 3 again. Called the elevator company line. Their tech is stuck in Portland, no way across tonight. You're down to one car for all floors. I've got pharmacy runners and a supply cart already lined up at the car on 2. How do you want me to run it?

House Sup, CNO, this is Rosalind Aguirre, staffing. Gulf Nurse Staffing just called back. The 14 relief nurses can't come until the bridge and the causeways reopen, and TxDOT won't inspect them until daylight. So 1:3 holds in the ICU and the NICU all night.

Second thing. 7 West needs a second RN on the 3 vented infants by the 23:00 break cycle. I don't have a name for it yet. And Dana K. and Luis M. are asking again to leave at the 23:00 shift change. Luis's wife has started having contractions. She's at home in Flour Bluff. I need answers on all of it before 23:00.

fields.voiceStyle: Lines 1–2: middle-aged male security officer, steady and clipped, a little rushed. Lines 3–4: female charge-level RN in her forties, tired, controlled, speaking quickly.

instructorNote: Purpose: two problems at once on landfall night, a single elevator and a staffing gap that will last all night. Look for the HS to take control of the one-car queue (critical-care moves and emergencies first, everything else by stairs), pull ride-out med-surg RNs from the ambulatory-wing pool to cover the 7 West vented infants, and send the more-than-3-short gap to the CNO within 15 minutes. The CNO should decide each release request openly and on the record, given that the roads are closed and leaving is unsafe, and Luis's wife can be directed to L&D on floor 4.
